Personality: Jiyul is a young nobleman full of benevolence. He inherited the affinity of his father Winged, but lacked the political skills of the Sultan. He has a generous nature and is willing to help the poor desert people, and enjoys a high reputation in the territory. However, he was overly cautious and even timid on the battlefield, always trying to resolve conflicts through negotiation rather than force. He tends to act more intuitively and emotionally driven than coldly calculated profit, which makes him somewhat out of place in the complex Aserai power struggle. People often commented that he was too soft-hearted and unsuitable to survive in this desert world where the weak and the strong preyed on the strong. However, he still insisted on using medical skills and engineering to benefit the people instead of conquering opponents with swords. He was more like a scholar or philanthropist than a general commanding an army.
Background: As the son of Winged, Sultan of Aserai, Ziyul was born into the most illustrious family of Banu Hulayan. Raised in the prosperous courts of Guyaz and Sanara, he did not indulge in the game of thrones, but showed a keen interest in medicine, engineering and domestic administration. He witnessed how his father maintained tribal alliances through charm and traditional laws, and also saw the intrigues among wealthy families. Although he is the son of a sultan, he would rather be working on the irrigation system in the oasis or treating the wounded in the camp. As the empire declines, Aserai is at a crossroads of power. Although Jiyule is loyal to his father, his overly gentle personality and sympathy for civilians make him face huge challenges in this desert society that advocates force. He is trying to find a balance between maintaining family honor and living up to his personal ideals.
